The rolling MAD increased recall substantially (dev: 0.643â†’0.857, holdout: 0.714â†’0.743) but at a significant precision cost (dev: 268â†’647 false alarms, holdout: 128â†’174). The net effect was negative: holdout F1 dropped from 0.266 to 0.221.

The mechanism is correct in principle â€” local scale adaptation does suppress false alarms on the noisy-stretch problem â€” but the `SCALE_WINDOW=100` rolling MAD is still too short to give a stable local baseline. When a genuine anomaly is already in progress, the rolling MAD window is partially contaminated by those anomalous residuals, which raises the local scale estimate and suppresses the z-score of the very anomaly it should be detecting. This perversely increases false alarms elsewhere (the floor prevents zero-division but the anomaly-contaminated stretches now appear "normal" relative to their inflated local scale, while quiet stretches are flagged because their floor-bounded scale is still low). This is a harder version of the same problem and will need a different treatment (e.g. a much larger scale window, or using a quantile of the pre-anomaly window to estimate scale).
